newsitem.title: UK: Greggs shares gain after upbeat statement.
newsitem.headline: Greggs shares gain after upbeat statement.

text.p: Shares in Greggs Plc jumped eight percent on Friday after the bakery retail group posted a sharp rise in annual pre-tax profit and said profit growth had accelerated in the second half of last year.
The stock was up 125p at 16.45 stg by 1220 GMT, some 23 percent higher than its level at the end of 1996.
Greggs said pre-tax profit rose 20 percent to 15.7 million stg in the year, comfortably exceeding its own budgets.
It said there had been a "significant acceleration" of profit growth in the second half, when pre-tax profit rose 26.7 percent compared with a 5.2 percent rise reported at the half-year stage.

"Our consistent progress has been based on our specialisation in bakery retailing, takeaway food and catering, and our focus on becoming the best and most profitable business in those fields," said chairman Ian Gregg.
"There is considerable potential for further growth by expanding our geographical coverage and progressively improving our proposition to the consumer. I therefore view our future with confidence."

The company said profits in the first nine weeks of 1997 were in line with its budgets and ahead of the previous year, and pointed out that first-half results would be compared with a period affected by both adverse weather and the onset of the "mad cow" scare.
Earnings per share rose 21.3 percent to 95.8p and the dividend was upped 23.1 percent to 32p per share. Sales were up 8.6 percent at 238.5 million stg.
During the year the company acquired bakery business Birketts with 57 stores in Cumbria, northern England and the Scottish borders.
